clue.text: Calculated to give the addict a start

definitions.text: Calculated to give the addict a start

parts.words: Calculated to give the addict a start
parts.note: the 'start' an addict needs is the beginning of a dependence, so something that sets one going on a routine of craving

explanation.surface: Something designed to launch a drug user on the road to dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug or practice that creates a dependency is said to be addictive in this compound sense.

clue.text: One of three by John Buchan

definitions.text: One of three by John Buchan

parts.words: One of three by John Buchan
parts.note: Buchan wrote a Richard Hannay thriller about three captives held for ransom

explanation.surface: Something counted among a trio by a Scottish thriller writer.
explanation.walkthrough: John Buchan's novel 'The Three Hostages' (1924) features his hero Richard Hannay; each captive is one of the three.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held as security, one of the three in the title of Buchan's Hannay novel.

clue.text: Bloomer? Could be a big one

definitions.text: Bloomer?

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word, so they are to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A blunder that may turn out to be a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a gaffe but is a flowering plant; 'Could be' asks for A BIG ONE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is something that blooms, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Situation taken by a coach

definitions.text: Situation taken by a coach

parts.note: a situation is a job, and a coach is a private teacher, so the post a private teacher holds

explanation.surface: A place occupied by a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or position of a private teacher, who coaches pupils.

clue.text: A word on the possessive case?

definitions.text: A word on the possessive case

parts.words: A word on the possessive case
parts.note: the possessive case is a grammar term, but read literally it is a case of possessing, and the word for the one who possesses

explanation.surface: A remark about grammar's genitive form.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who possesses something is its proprietor.

clue.text: A chap squared by the islander ?

definitions.text: the islander

parts.note: a chap is a man
'by' as in multiplication, written with the times sign X
squaring the chap multiplies him by himself, so he is written a second time

explanation.surface: A fellow cornered by an island native.
explanation.walkthrough: The islander is a native of the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea; a chap squared is MAN by MAN, written MAN X MAN with the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Even dead ones live

definitions.text: Even dead ones live

parts.note: plants called dead- versions are living weeds

explanation.surface: A paradox that even the departed go on living.
explanation.walkthrough: The dead-nettle is a living plant, so even 'dead' ones live.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinging weeds of the genus Urtica, whose non-stinging lookalikes are called 'dead'.

clue.text: A minute number of supporters

definitions.text: A minute

parts.note: sixty is one particular number, the one that matters for a minute
seconds are the attendants who support a duellist or boxer

explanation.surface: A tiny count of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as 'tiny' but is the unit of time; the number is the count of seconds in it, and seconds attend a boxer or duellist.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a unit of time lasting exactly that span.

clue.text: Not something to be on the lookout for ?

definitions.text: Not something to be on the lookout for ?

parts.words: Not something to be on the lookout for
parts.note: you need not keep watch for a thing that is already visible; the other sense is understanding that is not about looking at all

explanation.surface: A sentry is told what not to watch for.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words and the clue says the thing is already visible, so there is nothing to look out for; as one word it is perception of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceptive understanding is a mental seeing, not a watch kept with the eyes.

clue.text: The sort of train you won't catch unless you're in at the start

definitions.text: The sort of train you won't catch unless you're in at the start

parts.words: The sort of train you won't catch unless you're in at the start
parts.note: an express that makes no halts can only be boarded at its departure station

explanation.surface: Advice to a commuter about an express service.
explanation.definitionFit: An express that runs without halting between termini can be boarded only where its journey begins.

clue.text: "All the world and his wife" to Wesley

definitions.text: "All the world and his wife" to Wesley

parts.words: "All the world and his wife" to Wesley
parts.note: John Wesley said 'I look upon all the world as my parish', so everyone was a member of his congregation

explanation.surface: A preacher's view of everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wesley, founder of Methodism, declared 'I look upon all the world as my parish', so all the world and his wife were his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a parish congregation, and Wesley counted the whole world as his parish.

clue.text: It's the terrain that confuses him

definitions.text: him

indicators.note: to confuse the letters is to jumble them into a new order

explanation.surface: A rambler blames the ground for losing his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the definition: the man who coaches athletes or horses, perhaps on such ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach of athletes or racehorses is a person, so a 'him' fits the definition.

clue.text: Rose in need of speech-training ?

definitions.text: Rose
definitions.meaning: a climbing rose of a vigorous trailing kind

definitions.text: in need of speech-training ?
definitions.meaning: one who talks on and on, wandering from the point

explanation.surface: A flower name that sounds like it needs elocution lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose variety, and also a wandering talker whose discourse needs discipline.

clue.text: Biblical girl-graduate

definitions.text: Biblical

parts.note: she stands for a woman or girl
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A girl from the scriptures who has taken her degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biblical' stands for the biblical name, the kingdom whose Queen visited Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: The land whose queen visited Solomon is named in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Man is thus absorbed in man's affairs

definitions.text: Man is thus absorbed in man's affairs

indicators.note: the letters are taken up and reworked, like matters thrown together in business affairs

explanation.surface: A remark about human beings being wrapped up in their own concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MAN IS THUS rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes such thinkers: people absorbed in human concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of a philosophy centred on human rather than divine concerns.

clue.text: What some can drive others to become

definitions.text: What some can drive others to become

parts.words: What some can drive others to become
parts.note: 'drive' as in drive a car: some people's behaviour drives others to take up the wheel themselves

explanation.surface: People who can push others to the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: People who drive cars; those who can drive are, by definition, car users.

clue.text: It may give grounds for complaint

definitions.text: It may give grounds for complaint

parts.words: It may give grounds for complaint
parts.note: grounds are the dregs left after brewing; a vessel that leaves them in the cup gives literal grounds to grumble about

explanation.surface: Something that could justify a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewing jug for the dark drink made from roasted beans leaves sediment behind.

clue.text: Wearisome military duty

definitions.text: Wearisome military duty

parts.note: a soldier's menial non-combat work, which is also a word for tiredness

explanation.surface: Dull soldierly chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's manual non-combat duty bears the same name as exhaustion.

clue.text: Seven letters rolled into one

definitions.text: Seven letters rolled into one

parts.note: the answer has seven letters and is itself one letter, a formal written message

explanation.surface: Several messages combined in one scroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter, such as those of Paul in the New Testament, written as a single message.

clue.text: Does this corn need tropical conditions ?

definitions.text: Does this corn need tropical conditions ?

parts.words: Does this corn need tropical conditions
parts.note: put the answer in front of 'corn' and you get a sign of the zodiac whose name follows 'Tropic of'

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether a grain crop needs a hot climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' plus 'corn' makes CAPRICORN, and the Tropic of Capricorn is the 'tropical condition' it needs; the answer is also an Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's name joined to corn gives the tropic line south of the equator.

clue.text: Sympathise with an old monarch about his disorderly son

definitions.text: Sympathise with

indicators.note: the monarch's name goes about, around, the jumbled son

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: disorderly means the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Comforting an aged king whose boy is unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NSO, the jumble of SON signalled by 'disorderly', inside COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to show fellow feeling with them.

clue.text: Makes a turn-over on the land, but still fails

definitions.text: Makes a turn-over on the land
definitions.meaning: turns the soil of a field with a blade drawn by a tractor or horse

definitions.text: fails
definitions.meaning: British slang for failing an exam

explanation.surface: A farmer works the field but still falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to be 'ploughed' is to fail an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer turns furrows in soil; in British slang an examiner turning down a candidate does the same.

clue.text: The roundest of figures

definitions.text: The roundest of figures

parts.note: a round figure is a number ending in zeros, and the zero itself is the most perfectly round digit

explanation.surface: Praise for the most curvaceous shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, written as a circle, is the ultimate round number.

clue.text: Changing them affects the rates, especially for 15

definitions.text: Changing them affects the rates, especially for 15

parts.words: Changing them affects the rates, especially for 15
parts.note: 15 down is drivers, who change the toothed wheels of a car to alter its speed

explanation.surface: A remark on altering local taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' looks like British local taxes but means speeds; '15' refers to the answer of 15 down, car drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed wheels in a car's transmission that set the ratio of engine speed to road speed.

clue.text: "Can't you 'ear their paddles chunkin' from to Mandalay ?"(Kipling)

definitions.text: "Can't you 'ear their paddles chunkin' from to Mandalay ?"(Kipling)

parts.words: "Can't you 'ear their paddles chunkin' from to Mandalay ?"(Kipling)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Kipling's poem 'Mandalay': the gap is the Burmese port the paddle steamers sailed from

explanation.surface: A line of Kipling's verse with a place name missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash where the missing word goes; it is the old name of Yangon, Burma's chief port.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Burmese capital and port on the Irrawaddy delta, starting point of the river voyage.

clue.text: But not the classic weapon of the "Keystone Cops "

definitions.text: But not the classic weapon of the "Keystone Cops "

parts.words: But not the classic weapon of the "Keystone Cops "
parts.note: 'classic' means in Latin: the Latin word for an arrow, a weapon no slapstick silent-film policeman ever used

explanation.surface: A remark on what the bumbling silent-film police never carried.
explanation.walkthrough: The Keystone Cops were slapstick policemen of silent films, armed with truncheons and custard pies; the classical (Latin) weapon here is the arrow, also a constellation's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for arrow, also the name of a small northern constellation.

clue.text: Unlike Jackson he doesn't play for safety

definitions.text: Unlike Jackson he doesn't play for safety

parts.words: Unlike Jackson he doesn't play for safety
parts.note: General Jackson was nicknamed 'Stonewall', and in cricket a stonewaller blocks every ball; the opposite batsman hits out wildly

explanation.surface: A comparison of a player's style with a cautious one called Jackson.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'stonewaller' bats defensively, after Stonewall Jackson, the American Civil War general; the answer is the batsman who swings hard at everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who hits hard and recklessly, the opposite of a defensive blocker.

clue.text: Family of South Coast landladies ?

definitions.text: Family of South Coast landladies ?

parts.note: a row of chalk cliffs in Sussex, on England's south coast, bears a name suggesting a household of female siblings who own the land

explanation.surface: A group of related women running seaside guest houses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer names chalk cliffs near Eastbourne in Sussex, on England's south coast; as 'landladies' they are female relatives who are literally land.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalk cliffs between Seaford and Eastbourne carry a name that suggests a household of female siblings.
